answer.label: fine-tune backdoor
answer.justification: Only logit measurements are available, and no class fits every value cleanly; fine-tune backdoor is the least inconsistent. The raw-score shift ÷ TV of 4.3 ×10⁵ rules out fine-tune bias (10.4 ± 0.4). It also argues against quantization (2.3 ± 0.1), as does the Token-DiFR gap of 0.071, about 8 spreads above quantization's 0.038 ± 0.004. KL 0.094 and TV 0.061 are far below both system-prompt classes (KL 0.24–0.30, TV 0.12–0.14), which also show top-1 agreement of only 0.87–0.89 against 0.936 here. Against fine-tune backdoor, the gaps are moderate: KL 0.094 vs 0.153 ± 0.047, DiFR 0.071 vs 0.152 ± 0.051, sequence agreement 0.609 vs 0.521 ± 0.055 (each 1.3–1.6 spreads), and raw-score shift 4.3 vs 3.3 ± 0.3. Its weaker points are top-1 agreement (0.936 vs 0.909 ± 0.011) and TV (0.061 vs 0.086 ± 0.012), each 2–2.5 spreads off. Quantization is the main alternative given the low TV and high top-1 agreement. Without activation data (size ratio, onset layer), the call stays uncertain.
